title: Continuity of supported Kummer maps for preserved regular sequences
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $I$ be a small directed set and $(Z_i\hookrightarrow V_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine Noetherian schemes with affine transition maps. Suppose that for a fixed $c\geq0$ each $Z_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ is cut out by a regular sequence $t_{i,1},\ldots,t_{i,c}$, and every transition pulls these elements back to the corresponding elements at the next stage [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that $\ell$ is invertible on every $V_i$, that $V=\varprojlim_i V_i$ and $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ are Noetherian, and that the limiting sequence is regular and cuts out $Z\hookrightarrow V$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, canonical pullback gives
$$\varinjlim_i H^q_{Z_i}(V_i,A(m))\cong H^q_Z(V,A(m)),\qquad \varinjlim_i H^q(Z_i,A(m))\cong H^q(Z,A(m)).$$
Supported cohomology means the derived closed-support functor [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Under these identifications, the maps on cohomology induced by the supported Kummer classes of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus],
$$H^q(Z_i,A)\longrightarrow H^{q+2c}_{Z_i}(V_i,A(c)),$$
form a compatible system whose colimit is the same Kummer-class map for $Z\hookrightarrow V$. The transition maps need not be flat; the explicit preservation of the regular sequence is required.

source.place: Expose XVI, supported Cartier Kummer construction in section 2.1 and regular-sequence formula of Definition 2.3.1; base-change compatibility of Proposition 2.2.3.1 when the conormal data are preserved. Continuity: Stacks Project Tag 03Q6, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology, applied to the ambient, complement and closed schemes. The simultaneous supported and Kummer-map formulation is an agent-formulated consequence.

proof.text: Choose $i_0\in I$ and work on the cofinal tail $i\geq i_0$: an upper bound for $i_0$ and any given index shows cofinality. Write $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $J_{i,k}=(t_{i,1},\ldots,t_{i,k})$, $W_{i,k}=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i/J_{i,k})$, and $U_i=V_i-Z_i$. Preservation of the elements gives $J_{j,k}=J_{i,k}R_j$, hence $W_{j,k}=W_{i,k}\times_{V_i}V_j$ and $U_j=U_i\times_{V_i}V_j$. In $R=\varinjlim R_i$ the ideal generated by the limiting elements is the image of these ideals: a finite sum expressing membership lifts to some common stage. Thus $\varinjlim(R_i/J_{i,k})=R/(t_1,\ldots,t_k)$, so the analogous $W_k$ are their affine limits. Also $U=V-Z=U_{i_0}\times_{V_{i_0}}V$. Each $U_i$ is the finite union $\bigcup_{a=1}^cD(t_{i,a})$, with affine intersections, so is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; its transition maps are affine by this Cartesian description. For $c=0$, $Z_i=V_i$ and $U_i=\varnothing$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $t_{i,k}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R_i/J_{i,k-1}$, and likewise at the limit. Hence each $W_{i,k}\hookrightarrow W_{i,k-1}$ and $W_k\hookrightarrow W_{k-1}$ is an effective Cartier divisor. All these quotient schemes are Noetherian.

source.place: XVI, Definition 2.3.1 and the regular-generator Cartier flag; elementary affine ring calculation

proof.text: For every signed twist $m$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies the coefficient on every scheme in Step 1 with the pullback of its coefficient at $i_0$, compatibly with every transition and projection to the limit. These are torsion sheaves, killed by $\ell$. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] separately to $(V_i)$, $(U_i)$ and $(Z_i)$. Their index is small cofiltered in the inverse direction, the transitions are affine, and their terms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1. We obtain the canonical isomorphisms $\varinjlim H^r(V_i,A(m))\cong H^r(V,A(m))$, $\varinjlim H^r(U_i,A(m))\cong H^r(U,A(m))$ and $\varinjlim H^r(Z_i,A(m))\cong H^r(Z,A(m))$ for $r\geq0$. For $r<0$ both sides vanish since these are sheaves in degree zero. This proves the ordinary-cohomology assertion in every degree, without any flatness assumption.

Apply [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] with $T=B=V_i$, $C=Z_i$, $F=A(m)[0]$, and also at the limit. This gives the localization long exact sequences relating $H^r_{Z_i}(V_i,A(m))$, $H^r(V_i,A(m))$ and $H^r(U_i,A(m))$. The comparison maps are those of the natural shifted restriction cone in [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]: pullback on the ambient and open terms forms a commutative square, and the induced map on the shifted cone gives the supported pullback and commutes with its boundary. Thus these are compatible long exact sequences. Their filtered colimit is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. For each $q$ compare its five consecutive terms
$$H^{q-1}(V_i,A(m))\to H^{q-1}(U_i,A(m))\to H^q_{Z_i}(V_i,A(m))\to H^q(V_i,A(m))\to H^q(U_i,A(m))$$
with the limit sequence. The four ordinary terms have isomorphisms by Step 2. Exactness expresses the middle term as an extension of the cokernel of the first arrow by the kernel of the last. The induced maps on that cokernel and kernel are isomorphisms, so the middle map is an isomorphism: an element of its kernel comes from the left cokernel and vanishes there, and a target element lifts first from the right kernel and then corrects by the left cokernel. Consequently the canonical map $\varinjlim H^q_{Z_i}(V_i,A(m))\to H^q_Z(V,A(m))$ is an isomorphism. Negative groups vanish as right derived functors of a left exact functor on a degree-zero sheaf.

proof.text:
Use $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$ in [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. Its regular-generator formula identifies the specified class for $Z_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ with the ordered composite of the supported Cartier Kummer maps for $W_{i,k}\hookrightarrow W_{i,k-1}$, and gives the same description at the limit. More precisely, [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] extends each Cartier operator to the closed support $Z_i\subset W_{i,k}$, giving
$$T_{i,k}:H^a_{Z_i}(W_{i,k},A(b))\longrightarrow H^{a+2}_{Z_i}(W_{i,k-1},A(b+1)).$$
Its supported-Hom clause identifies the nested products with composition of the supported morphisms. Starting from $H^q_{Z_i}(W_{i,c},A)=H^q(Z_i,A)$, apply $T_{i,c}$, then $T_{i,c-1}$, down to $T_{i,1}$. The resulting $G_i=T_{i,1}\circ\cdots\circ T_{i,c}$ is exactly the map in the item, with target $H^{q+2c}_{Z_i}(V_i,A(c))$. Define $G$ at the limit in precisely the same way. For $c=0$ the composite is the identity, as required by the class-calculus normalization.

source.place: XVI, section 2.1, Definition 2.3.1 and Theorem 2.3.2, Cartier-flag formula

proof.text: Let $v:V_j\to V_i$ be a transition, or let $v:V\to V_i$ be a limit projection. For each $k$, Step 1 identifies its quotient square with the scheme-theoretic pullback square for the Cartier divisor $W_{i,k}\subset W_{i,k-1}$. The target divisor remains Cartier by regularity of the preserved sequence. Therefore [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies the pulled-back supported Cartier morphism with the Cartier morphism on that target. This is the theorem's arbitrary-morphism clause; it does not require $v$ to be flat. The pullback compatibility of the nested action products in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] then gives, on support $Z$, $v^*T_{i,k}(x)=T_{j,k}(v^*x)$, with $j$ replaced by the limit for a projection. The canonical twist comparisons used here are compatible with composition and tensor by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Substitute this equality successively for $k=c,c-1,\ldots,1$ into the composite of Step 4 to obtain $v^*G_i(x)=G_j(v_Z^*x)$, and also $v^*G_i(x)=G(v_Z^*x)$ at the limit. For $c=0$ these equations are simply functoriality of pullback.

source.place: XVI, section 2.1, naturality of supported Cartier Kummer operators along Cartier-preserving pullback; compare Proposition 2.2.3.1

proof.text:
Step 5 for transitions makes the $G_i$ a morphism of directed systems. Let $[x_i]\in\varinjlim_iH^q(Z_i,A)$. By Step 2 its image is $p_{i,Z}^*x_i\in H^q(Z,A)$; by Step 3 the image of $[G_i(x_i)]$ is $p_i^*G_i(x_i)$. The projection equation of Step 5 says exactly
$$p_i^*G_i(x_i)=G(p_{i,Z}^*x_i).$$
Every element of a directed colimit has such a representative, so under the two canonical continuity isomorphisms $\varinjlim G_i=G$. This is equality for the specified Kummer-class map, including the positive Cartier normalization fixed in Step 4, and proves every assertion.
